examples.text: 뭔가 착오가 있었을 겁니다, 다시 취재해 보세요. 우리 신디가 열네 살 때부터 한 얘긴데 설마 사실이 아니겠어요?
examples.trans: There must be some mistake—check again! Our Cindy has told that story since she was fourteen; how could it possibly be untrue?
The topic of mistake, mix-up came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: repeating an action or returning to a previous state

examples.trans: Please say that one more time.
I'll come back in a moment.

examples.text: 뭔가 착오가 있었을 겁니다, 다시 취재해 보세요. 우리 신디가 열네 살 때부터 한 얘긴데 설마 사실이 아니겠어요?
examples.trans: There must be some mistake—check again! Our Cindy has told that story since she was fourteen; how could it possibly be untrue?

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 취재하다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (report / check the story).

보다.gloss: to see, to watch; to take (an exam)

meanings.en: to see, to look at, to watch
meanings.note: Primary meaning.
Idiomatic in 시험을 보다.

examples.trans: I watched a movie on the weekend.
I took the driver's license exam.
I want to opens right now.
How about trying to opens together tomorrow?
I live in Seoul.
Where do you live?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 사는데요, 삽니다)
Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

examples.text: 선? 검사? 설마 검사가 예쁘기까지 하겠어?
examples.trans: A blind date? A prosecutor? Could a prosecutor really be pretty too?

examples.text: 설마 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (surely not, could it be), we will get good results.
See you at the shoot!

examples.text: 저도 뵌 적은 없어요, 늘 우리 신디를 통해서 듣기만 했죠.
examples.trans: I have never met them in person either—I always only heard about them through our Cindy.

meanings.note: bound noun used in -(으)ㄴ 적이 있다/없다 ('have/haven't ever done')

examples.trans: Have you ever been to Korea?

examples.text: 그런 말은 처음 들어 본 적이 있어요.
examples.trans: I've heard something like that before.

examples.text: 걱정은 하지, 늘. 근데 왜 백승찬을 집에 자꾸 들이냐?
examples.trans: I always worry. Still, why do you keep letting Baek Seung-chan into the house?

examples.text: 늘 준비하면 좋은 결과가 있을 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (always), we will get good results.

meanings.en: to go through, to communicate, to make sense
meanings.note: Often used as -를 통해서 to mean 'through (someone/something)'.

examples.trans: I heard it through a friend.
We can't communicate.

meanings.note: Interrogative adverb.

examples.trans: Why are you running?
Why were you late today?
I want to surprised right now.
How about trying to surprised together tomorrow?

examples.text: 어, 그래! 솔직히 너랑 있으니까 참 편하더라고.
examples.trans: Yeah, sure! Honestly, having you around has been super convenient.

examples.text: 네가 말은 안 해도 그렇게 속으로 나를 위하는구나 하면서 솔직히 감동도 하고 매니저라는 직업이 보람된 일이구나 그랬는데…
examples.trans: I was honestly touched thinking you cared for me deep down without saying so, and felt how rewarding being a manager is…

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 아니요, 저는 검사가 아니라 증인으로서 예진 선배님께 진실을 전달할 겁니다.
examples.trans: No, not as a prosecutor—as a witness, I intend to deliver the truth to Senior Ye-jin.
Here the word for 'the truth' is key.
I want to humbly tell him right now.
How about trying to humbly tell him together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

examples.text: 왜? 신디야, 놀랄 거 없어. 기자님한테 솔직히 진실만 말씀드리면 되지, 네가 떳떳한데 쫄 게 뭐 있어?
examples.trans: Why? Nothing to panic over, Cindy—just tell the reporter the honest truth. If your conscience is clear, why be afraid?
The mood on set today is truly conscience is clear, so.

examples.text: 왜? 신디야, 놀랄 거 없어. 기자님한테 솔직히 진실만 말씀드리면 되지, 네가 떳떳한데 쫄 게 뭐 있어?
examples.trans: Why? Nothing to panic over, Cindy—just tell the reporter the honest truth. If your conscience is clear, why be afraid?

examples.text: 이번에는 꼭 제대로 해 보고 싶어요, 쫄다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: This time I really want to do it right (cower, be intimidated).

meanings.note: loanword from English 'camera'

examples.trans: Please move the camera over here.
I bought a new camera.
I want to turned off and right now.
How about trying to turned off and together tomorrow?

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)
